checks: Verified the revised frozen byte digest and compared every decoded field to the original. Only the statement changed, and its only change is to specify a finite list of prescribed caps for each fiber. With finitely many fibers and a positive per-cap guard, the minimum positive guard is positive whenever any caps are prescribed. Thus one mesh works for all cap guards simultaneously.

Verified both source digests and checked 9ebcb0d70f814565 §7 (7) and conclusion, and ec0876d0e4a0084f §§3–4. The frozen proof replaces the earlier potential-locality appeal with a direct Green argument and an L² projection.

On an interval shorter than π, Poincaré gives coercive Q; nodal sine interpolation gives the exact Q-projection by cellwise integration by parts, and smooth density plus the projection norm bound gives strong convergence.

The proposed Green kernel for −D²−1 has zero endpoints, a derivative jump of −1 and positive interior kernel. The sign of h−Ph and the two endpoint derivative integrals follow. Nonatomic curvature gives continuous derivatives on the arc, including the matching original outer derivative at each gluing endpoint.

The area difference is minus one half the residual norm-square difference because the endpoint-homogeneous cross term vanishes. The global H¹ formula includes the glued facets. Nonnegative curvature gives a periodic support, and uniform convergence preserves interior.

At any fixed guarded line, one-sided derivative convergence keeps each whole new exposed face on the required side. The boundary paths share the exterior arc and its endpoints. Their winding difference vanishes in the opposite halfplane, so the cap-area change there is zero and on the arc side is the full area change. The minimum of the finite positive margins gives this simultaneously on the same sufficiently fine mesh.

The finite extreme Jensen gaps all have form D+κf. For κ<0 a nonnegative gap is concave and an interior zero forces identity. For κ=0 use ODE uniqueness at a zero minimum. For κ>0 the first and last zeros are legitimate by compactness and the positive Green kernel excludes source mass between them. Singleton zero sets and endpoints have zero mass by nonatomicity. All nonidentity gaps are simultaneously strict on an open set of full source measure, so a compact guard with a positive restricted source exists.

If f agreed with a homogeneous function on the support of the restricted nonatomic source, its difference would have zero values at the two extreme support points. The Green formula makes it strictly negative in between because there is positive source mass there, contradicting the existence of an interior support point. Thus the L² projection yields a bounded density with both moments zero and strictly negative pairing with f.

Variation of constants gives the required signed source, and the two moments make the potential vanish after its support. The common sine interpolant of this potential is supported in the guard on fine meshes. The positive square-root expression solves 2Aξ+Bξ²=E exactly, gives ξ→0, preserves identities, and controls every other Jensen gap by its guard margin.

At interior nodes the signed correction jumps are bounded by the interpolated positive-source jumps, including at zero atoms. At endpoints there is no correction. In the at-most-three branch, common domination and the Green formula make all residuals strictly negative inside the interval; the rank lemma gives the exhaustive independent/proportional split, with the smooth specialization obtained by finite common bounds against Lebesgue measure.

Same-batch exact tensor rank criterion. Applied to a nonempty set of at most three distinct base points with nonzero real residual functions in H₀¹. In the dependent case these residuals are proportional with positive scalars because their continuous representatives are strictly negative at every interior point. The criterion passes the independent proof read.

Same-batch revised tensor-affine theorem, approved on its exact revised hashes. In the independent branch the base is nonempty and finite, the fibers satisfy every Jensen inequality, and the interval, common nonatomic domination, inward endpoint accumulation, finite cap lists with strict margins, and independent tensors are exactly the revised theorem hypotheses.

issues.defect: The stated margin is quantified for each cap on the whole arc, but there is neither a finite cap count nor an explicit common margin across all caps. A single unit disk on a proper interval satisfies all the other hypotheses. For q in a countable dense subset of the interval interior and integers m≥1, prescribe H_{q,m}={x:x·u(q)≤1+1/m}. Each original arc lies strictly inside its cap, with distance at least 1/m. Each original cap area is the full disk area. The same cap and total areas force a new convex body with interior to lie in every H_{q,m}; otherwise an open subset of its interior would lie outside a cap. Continuity in q and the unchanged exterior support force inclusion in the unit disk. Equal area then forces equality with the disk, whose support 1 is nowhere homogeneous on any nonempty open cell.
issues.locator: Cap-guard assumption in Statement and simultaneous conclusion in Caps and fixed endpoints
issues.repair: Explicitly require finitely many prescribed caps per fiber, or quantify one positive lower bound over all prescribed cap lines and the corresponding arcs. Then uniform convergence controls the guards simultaneously.

overlap.comparison: Provides exact polygonal reconstruction for a single body from finitely many rays and sector areas. It leaves the body free between and outside those sectors and supplies no arbitrary exterior-support preservation or coupled Jensen constraints.

Preserves cap areas for finitely many concurrent lines in a single-body radial saturation problem. It does not replace a local normal arc while fixing its exterior support or jointly enforcing compatibility.

initial_review.readability: The direct rank-one case requires no inward support accumulation because its correction is compactly supported in the interior. The at-most-three branch needs inward accumulation for the invoked tensor-affine method.
initial_review.summary: The compactly supported scalar correction is valid for a finite cap list or a common cap margin. The frozen cap guard is insufficient for an unrestricted list, and the at-most-three branch also needs independent approval of the corrected tensor-affine predecessor.
